I traced both comments through the code. The first one is a real bug, but your test went down a different path. You're right that the second one doesn't submit the form. I couldn't run it end to end because no backend is running on port 9000, so this is from reading the code.

## Comment 1 (removed org can't be picked again): correct, but only when editing a saved tag

[TagConfigForm.tsx](/Users/jacob/Desktop/care_fe/src/pages/Admin/TagConfig/TagConfigForm.tsx:476) sets `currentOrganizations` from `existingConfig.organization`. That prop never changes after you remove the org, and [handleSelect](/Users/jacob/Desktop/care_fe/src/components/Common/RoleOrgSelector.tsx:69) checks it to decide whether an org is already selected. To reproduce:

1. Edit a tag that already has organization A saved.
2. Click ✕. The list is now empty and the form value is `null`.
3. Open the picker and click A. Because A is still in `currentOrganizations`, the picker shows **"Already selected"** (disabled) and returns without adding A.
4. A is still not selected, so saving clears the organization.

In your test you added a *new* org and then clicked ✕. That org isn't in `currentOrganizations`, so the check never applies.

What you saw (the picker still showing the earlier item) is a separate stale-state bug. `handleSelect` calls `handleConfirmSelection` (which clears `currentSelection`) and then sets `currentSelection` back to the org. `handleRemoveOrganization` never clears it, so after ✕ the picker still shows the removed org's name.

A small fix would handle both:
- Check the duplicate against `selectedOrganizations` instead of `currentOrganizations` in `handleSelect` and in `isDisabled`.
- Call `setCurrentSelection(null)` in `handleRemoveOrganization`.

## Comment 2 (Remove button submits the form): not a bug in practice

The review is right that the remove button has no `type`, and the shared [Button](/Users/jacob/Desktop/care_fe/src/components/ui/button.tsx:75) doesn't set one. So it is a native submit button inside the `<form>`. It doesn't submit because:

- The only consumer uses `singleSelection`, so clicking ✕ removes that row, including the button.
- React applies that change before the browser runs the button's default submit action. By then the button is no longer in the form, so nothing is submitted.

It's only masked, though. If the button stayed on the page after the click, it would submit. That could happen in multi-select mode: rows use `key={index}`, so removing a row that isn't the last keeps the clicked button on the page. Adding `type="button"` is a one-line safeguard, but it isn't a bug in this PR.

I haven't edited anything. I can apply the Comment 1 fix, and optionally the `type="button"`, if you'd like.
